_readme: Elton draft. [[c:...]] is cyan = not confirmed. History from the Elton Parish Council short history unless noted.
name: School Lane

layers.essential_history: [[c:School Lane used to be called Church Lane. It was renamed in 1876, when a new school for boys and girls opened here.]]
layers.deeper_history: [[c:An earlier boys' school was built in 1727, and a girls' school once met in the old women's workhouse, paid for by Lady Jane Proby's will in 1712.]]
layers.mystery: [[c:This lane was once called Church Lane. The parish clerk left a note about who was in the church that night, written backwards so the soldiers couldn't read it.]]

sources.title: Elton Parish Council: A short history of Elton

directions_to_next: [[c:Head south, about 170 metres as the crow flies, to All Saints Church. Follow School Lane to the church at the end. Keep to the pavements and paths.]]

puzzle.title: [[c:The clerk's mirror note]]
puzzle.question: [[c:What was Mistress Carey doing at midnight? (one word)]]
hints: [[c:Start at the end of the line.]]
[[c:The last word, read backwards, is MISTRESS.]]
puzzle.reveal: [[c:It reads MISTRESS CAREY WAS PRAYING AT MIDNIGHT. She was in the church, not at the ford.]]

evidence: [[c:Mistress Carey was praying in the church at midnight. The clerk saw her.]]
